key_insight: Hydrogen in bcc iron not only lowers yield stress, but also stabilizes a multimodal high-index twin network by prolonging {112} twin variants and suppressing detwinning.
engineering_relevance: This suggests hydrogen can strongly alter hardening, twinning pathways, and failure-relevant deformation behavior in iron-based structural materials.
method: Comparison of pure bcc Fe versus Fe with 10% hydrogen across loading, temperature, and tension/compression
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation evidence that hydrogen and temperature change twin variant persistence, detwinning, and the emergence of {332}-{10 9 3} and {7 4 1} twin boundaries under different loading paths.
watch_item: Results are based on atomistic simulation with a specific hydrogen concentration, so transferability to real microstructures, defect populations, and lower H levels may require experimental validation.
paper_title: Hydrogen-stabilized multimodal high-index twin network in iron
